title: Thames River Cruise Departure Piers: Complete London Boarding Guide
metaTitle: Thames River Cruise Departure Piers: 2026 London Boarding Guide
metaDescription: Find all major Thames river cruise departure piers in London, including Westminster, London Eye, Tower, and Greenwich, with Tube lines and boarding tips.
excerpt: Looking for where your boat departs? Discover London's main Thames river cruise departure piers, how to get there by Tube, and essential pier boarding tips.
quickAnswer: The primary Thames river cruise departure piers in central London are Westminster Pier (directly beside Big Ben and Westminster Underground), London Eye Pier (Waterloo / South Bank), Tower Millennium Pier (next to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge), and Greenwich Pier (beside Cutty Sark). Sightseeing cruises offer both 40-minute circular loops and point-to-point routes between Westminster and Greenwich. Always verify the pier printed on your boarding ticket and arrive 15 minutes before departure.
author: Camille Dubois / Senior London Travel Editor
imageAlt: Thames river cruise departure piers: sightseeing boat docked at Westminster Millennium Pier beside the River Thames
content:
Knowing the key Thames river cruise departure piers across central London is the secret to a smooth river sightseeing day. While the River Thames flows right through historic London, embarkation piers are spread across several distinct riverside zones, from Big Ben to maritime Greenwich.

Heading to the wrong pier can leave you rushing across bridges or missing your scheduled boat. Whether your ticket specifies Westminster, the London Eye, Tower Pier, or Greenwich, this guide covers every primary Thames river cruise boarding location, nearby Tube stations, and practical tips. If you are comparing ticket styles before choosing your pier, explore our Thames cruise ticket price comparison or read our guide on how to book Thames cruise tickets online.

1. Westminster Millennium Pier (Beside Big Ben & Parliament)

Situated at the foot of Westminster Bridge on Victoria Embankment, Westminster Millennium Pier is the busiest boarding point on the River Thames.

Why Depart From Westminster?

Westminster is the quintessential starting point for London visitors. From the floating pontoon, you enjoy an unbeatable view of the Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben) and Parliament.

  • Popular routes: 40- to 60-minute circular sightseeing loops returning to Westminster, or one-way voyages downriver to Tower Pier and Greenwich.
  • How to get there: Take the Underground to Westminster Station (Jubilee, District, and Circle lines). Exit 1 or 2 is just 50 metres from the pier steps.
  • Nearby landmarks: Westminster Abbey, Parliament Square, and Whitehall.

2. London Eye Pier (Waterloo & South Bank)

Located on the South Bank directly beneath the observation wheel, London Eye Pier (Waterloo Millennium Pier) is a vibrant departure spot in the middle of London's cultural district.

  • Best for: Sightseers pairing a river cruise with a flight on the London Eye or exploring the Southbank Centre.
  • Route highlights: Boats sail east past Shakespeare's Globe, Tate Modern, and St Paul's Cathedral toward Tower Bridge.
  • How to get there: A 5-minute walk from Waterloo Station (Bakerloo, Northern, Jubilee lines) or across the Golden Jubilee Bridges from Charing Cross.

3. Tower Millennium Pier (Beside Tower Bridge & Tower of London)

If you want to board in the historic City of London, Tower Millennium Pier offers a dramatic river approach.

Boarding by Tower Bridge

Tower Pier sits immediately adjacent to the ancient stone walls of the Tower of London. Boarding here lets you sail directly beneath the twin gothic towers of Tower Bridge within seconds of leaving the dock.

  • Best for: Travellers finishing a morning visit to the Crown Jewels wanting a river cruise back to Westminster or toward Greenwich.
  • How to get there: Underground to Tower Hill Station (District and Circle lines, 5-minute walk) or Tower Gateway DLR.
  • Atmosphere: Energetic and scenic, with wide viewing platforms and electronic boarding boards.

4. Greenwich Pier (Cutty Sark & Royal Naval College)

Located roughly six miles downriver from Westminster, Greenwich Pier is the gateway to London's UNESCO maritime quarter.

Maritime Greenwich from the Water

Cruising to Greenwich Pier is considered the single most rewarding river itinerary in London. As your vessel passes Canary Wharf, the twin domes of the Old Royal Naval College open up majestically.

  • Nearby sights: The 1869 tea clipper Cutty Sark, National Maritime Museum, and Royal Observatory on Greenwich hill.
  • How to get there: Take the DLR to Cutty Sark for Maritime Greenwich, just 2 minutes from the pier.

5 Practical Boarding Tips for Thames River Cruises

1. Arrive at Least 15 Minutes Early

Thames sightseeing vessels run to strict timetables and river licensing slots. Boarding gates open 15 minutes before departure, and queues form early on peak days.

2. Check Your Pier Gate Letter

Major piers like Westminster and Tower have multiple floating boarding pontoons with lettered gangways (e.g., Gate A, B, or C). Check your voucher to queue at the correct gate.

3. Sightseeing Cruise vs. Commuter Boats

Do not confuse sightseeing cruises with commuter river buses (Uber Boat). Commuter boats operate on rapid transit schedules without commentary, whereas sightseeing cruises feature live or audio commentary and open sundeck seating.

4. Weather & Indoor Heating

Thames sightseeing boats feature heated enclosed saloons with panoramic windows alongside open-top decks, keeping you warm and dry regardless of London weather.

5. Pushchair Accessibility

Sightseeing vessels accommodate foldable pushchairs, prams, and backpacks. Large suitcases cannot be taken onboard; use station lockers at Waterloo or Victoria if needed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where do most Thames river cruises depart from?
The two primary piers are Westminster Millennium Pier (beside Big Ben) and Tower Millennium Pier (beside Tower Bridge), with boats departing every 30 to 40 minutes.

Can I board a Thames cruise at the London Eye?
Yes, London Eye Pier sits directly underneath the observation wheel on the South Bank, offering regular departures toward Tower Bridge and Greenwich.

Do Thames river cruises return to the same pier?
You can book circular loops that return to your starting pier, or one-way routes (such as Westminster to Greenwich) that let you explore a new area.

How early should I get to the pier?
Plan to arrive 15 minutes before your departure time, or 20 minutes early on sunny weekends.

Summary: Which Thames Pier Should You Choose?

Selecting the right Thames river cruise departure piers depends on your day's plan:

  • Visiting Big Ben or Parliament? Depart from Westminster Millennium Pier.
  • Visiting Tower Bridge or the Tower of London? Board at Tower Millennium Pier.
  • Riding the London Eye or exploring South Bank? Head to London Eye Pier.
  • Planning a maritime day trip? Cruise down to Greenwich Pier for historic parks and royal heritage.

Winding through the heart of London, the River Thames has carried Londoners and visitors alike for two thousand years, and today it offers one of the best ways to see the city — gliding past the Houses of Parliament, the London Eye, and under the iconic Tower Bridge, all without fighting traffic or crowds on the pavement.

Because so many operators run cruises from several different piers, planning your trip requires a little preparation. Between choosing a departure pier, deciding between a daytime sightseeing cruise or an evening cruise with live music, and picking the right ticket tier, arriving unprepared can mean a rushed or disappointing experience. In this 2026 travel guide, we break down every cruise option, compare them side by side, and share the details that make the difference between a good cruise and a great one.

💡

Quick Summary for 2026 Visitors: The 1-Hour Sightseeing Cruise from Westminster is what most first-time visitors want — it passes Big Ben, the London Eye, and Tower Bridge in a single round trip. Book your exact departure time online — popular sailings can sell out 2 to 3 days in advance during peak season (June through September).

Understanding 2026 Thames Cruise Options

When booking a Thames river cruise, it helps to understand the different styles on offer. Cruises range from a simple sightseeing round trip to guided cruises with live commentary, evening cruises with live music, and specialty options like the afternoon tea cruise.

Why Booking Your Departure Time Matters in 2026

Thames cruise operators run boats on a fixed schedule to manage capacity and crew safely. Here is how the system works:

  • Exact Departure Windows: When you purchase a Thames river cruise ticket, you are assigned a specific sailing time (e.g., 10:00 AM, 1:30 PM, 7:00 PM).

  • Boarding Cutoff: Arrive at the pier 15 minutes before departure — boats leave on schedule and do not wait for latecomers.

  • Peak Season Demand: Weekend afternoons and summer evenings are the most popular sailings and can sell out 2–3 days ahead.

Top Landmarks You Will See Along the Way

A Thames cruise passes some of London's most recognizable sights, whichever pier you depart from.

1. Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament

Most cruises departing Westminster Pier pass directly beneath the Houses of Parliament, with Big Ben's clock tower rising above the water — one of the most photographed views in London.

The undisputed highlight for most passengers — sailing directly beneath the Victorian bascule bridge's twin towers is a moment every cruise builds toward.

4. Shakespeare's Globe and the Southbank

The reconstructed Globe Theatre, Tate Modern, and the bustling Southbank walkway line the river's south bank for much of the route.

Which Pier Should You Depart From?

Choosing your departure pier is straightforward using the London Underground network:

Westminster Pier

The most popular starting point, a 2-minute walk from Westminster Underground station. Cruises heading downstream from here cover the widest range of landmarks in a single loop.

Tower Pier

A 5-minute walk from Tower Hill station, right beside the Tower of London. Ideal if you're combining your cruise with a Tower of London or Tower Bridge visit.

Greenwich Pier

Next to Cutty Sark DLR station — the destination for round-trip cruises heading downstream to historic Greenwich.

Suggested Half-Day Thames Itinerary

To make the most of a Thames cruise alongside nearby sights, follow this sample itinerary:

  • 10:00 AM: Arrive at Westminster Pier ahead of your sailing.

  • 10:15 AM – 11:15 AM: 1-hour sightseeing cruise past Big Ben, the London Eye, and Tower Bridge.

  • 11:30 AM – 12:30 PM: Explore the Southbank and Borough Market for lunch.

  • 1:00 PM – 2:00 PM: Visit the Tower Bridge Exhibition.

  • 2:30 PM: Optional round-trip cruise onward to Greenwich.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can I buy Thames cruise tickets at the pier on the day?

Yes, most piers sell walk-up tickets, but popular sailings — especially weekend afternoons and summer evenings — frequently sell out. Purchasing your Thames cruise tickets online in advance guarantees your departure time and often costs less than buying at the pier.

What is the difference between a sightseeing cruise and an evening cruise?

The sightseeing cruise runs during the day with live commentary pointing out landmarks. The evening cruise departs after dark with live music instead of commentary, showing off the illuminated skyline.

Is photography permitted onboard?

Yes — photography is welcome throughout the cruise, and the open-air upper deck offers the best unobstructed shots of the landmarks.

How much time should I allocate for a Thames cruise?

A standard round-trip sightseeing cruise takes about an hour. Add a Greenwich stop and you're looking at 2–3 hours; the full-day combo with Tower Bridge takes 6–7 hours.

title: River Thames Cruises: The Complete 2026 Visitor Guide
metaTitle: River Thames Cruises Guide 2026 | Tickets, Departures & Tips
metaDescription: Complete 2026 guide to cruising the River Thames. Discover departure piers, ticket options, landmark views, and how to avoid sold-out sailings.
excerpt: Everything you need to know about cruising the River Thames: tickets, departure piers, what you'll see, and essential tips for your trip.
author: Camille Dubois / Thames Travel Writer
imageAlt: A Thames sightseeing boat passing the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben, London
content:
Flowing through the heart of London, the River Thames offers one of the most relaxing and scenic ways to see the city. Whether it's your first visit or your tenth, a river cruise reveals the capital's skyline — old and new — from an angle you simply can't get on foot.

Why Cruising the Thames Is an Unmissable Experience

A Thames cruise isn't just a scenic ride — it's a moving tour through two thousand years of London history. From the Houses of Parliament to Tower Bridge, the river ties together the city's most iconic landmarks into one relaxed outing.

💡
Pro Tip: Popular departure times can sell out 2 to 3 days ahead in peak season. Booking your cruise ticket in advance is the safest way to secure your preferred sailing.

What You Will See During Your Cruise

  • ✓Big Ben & the Houses of Parliament: Sail directly beneath London's most famous clock tower.
  • ✓The London Eye: See the giant observation wheel from river level.
  • ✓Tower Bridge: Pass beneath the Victorian bascule bridge's twin towers.
  • ✓The Southbank & Shakespeare's Globe: Glide past the reconstructed theatre and bustling riverside walkway.

Essential Practical Info for Your Cruise

Before heading to the pier, keep these guidelines in mind:

  • Total Cruise Time: 1 hour for a standard sightseeing round trip; 2–3 hours if adding a Greenwich stop.
  • Operating Hours: Cruises typically run 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM in summer, with evening sailings from 7:00 PM.
  • Departure Piers: Westminster Pier, Tower Pier, and Greenwich Pier are the three main starting points.
  • Dress Code: None required — a light jacket is recommended even in summer, as the river can be breezy.
  • Boarding: Arrive 15 minutes before your scheduled departure.
